To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) the GTP and GWP have similar numerical values for most gases and for a wide range (20?yr to 500?yr) of time-horizon, (2) the integrated GTP (iGTPX) and GWP are closely linked, and (3) the GWP represents, for many gases, a robust, transparent, and policy-relevant measure for comparing the climate change impacts of different gases.

(1) the integrated AGTP (iAGTP) and absolute global warming potential (AGWP) are closely linked, (2) the iGTP is a good proxy for the AGWP, except for very-short-lived species, and (3) the GTP is a good approximation for the iGTP.
(1) iGTP is similar to GWP, (2) iGTP and AGTP are linked, and (3) iGTP depends on the time-horizon over which integrated global temperature change is considered.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the relationships between the absolute and relative GTP, iGTP, and AOHP.
the question of what is the best way to compare the global warming potential of different greenhouse gases.
understanding the linkages and relationships between emission and climate metrics.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the GWP and iGTP are similar, but not identical, emission metrics that are both consistent with the objectives of the Kyoto Protocol.

the integrated global temperature change metric is the most relevant metric for climate policy and should be used in all cases, and that the global warming potential is a good substitute in most cases.
the GWP is not a perfect metric, but it is a useful one.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the integrated AGTP is a more robust metric for comparing emissions than the AGWP.
the GWP is the best metric for comparing emissions of long-lived species and the iGTP is the best metric to compare emissions of short-lived species.
the iGWP is a good proxy for iAGTP.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the GWP and iGTP are closely linked for a wide range (but not all) of GHGs and are both useful metrics for assessing emissions.
it is not necessary to choose between the GTP and the iGTP.
there are strong linkages among emission metrics and the interpretation of the emission metrics is dependent on how they are used.
